title: Integral alteration diagram with its specified proper covering witness
statement: Let $S$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-integral-scheme] and $I$ an index type. An integral alteration diagram over $S$, indexed by $I$, consists of integral Noetherian schemes $T_i$ and $P$ (Noetherian means quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]), dominant finite-type maps $f_i:T_i\to S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], a proper surjective map $g:P\to S$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism], open subschemes $U_i\subseteq P$ [def-weil-open-immersion] with $\bigcup_iU_i=P$, and maps $h_i:U_i\to T_i$ satisfying $f_i h_i=g|_{U_i}$. Dominant means dense image. Require that each $f_i$ and $g$ has finite canonical function-field extension: the algebra of generic stalks induced by its dominant morphism [def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map] is finitely generated as a module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The index is finite when this datum is used in the spreading theorem, but the datum itself allows arbitrary $I$. For two such diagrams $D/S$ and $E/R$ and $s:S\to R$, a cartesian comparison means maps $t_i:D.T_i\to E.T_i$, $p:D.P\to E.P$, and $v_i:D.U_i\to E.U_i$ such that the squares $(t_i,D.f_i,E.f_i,s)$, $(p,D.g,E.g,s)$, and $(v_i,D.U_i\hookrightarrow D.P,E.U_i\hookrightarrow E.P,p)$ are fibre-product squares [def-pc-fibre-product], and $E.h_i v_i=t_i D.h_i$. This identifies $D$ with the base change of the entire specified diagram $E$, including its indexed open cover and every arrow.
